A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same authors' spectral analysis of attention, despite the revised title and organization. The complete main texts, figures, equations, proofs, and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original spectral, stable-rank, gradient, and Heaviside-function training experiments, including supplementary gradient experiments in Appendix A.3.

after.justification: V2 reports original initialization experiments, including BERT-family rank-collapse diagnostics, attention spectra, and comparisons of single-outlier and SVD-based outlier removal.

M1.justification: The central attention modification, A minus the uniform attention matrix, remains unchanged. V2 additionally implements an experimental SVD-based variant that removes the leading r singular components, selecting r by the largest consecutive singular-value gap (Appendix A.4). V1 only suggested removing additional outliers as future work.

E1.justification: V2 removes the synthetic Heaviside-function learning task entirely. It adds a distinct initialization scenario using tokenized sentences from the paper's abstract in BERT, ALBERT, and RoBERTa (Figure 3), extending beyond the earlier synthetic orthonormal-input experiments.

E2.justification: V2 adds the SVD-based 'no outliers' comparator in Figure 7 and ReLU/sigmoid attention to the spectral comparison in Figure 1. Xavier and upscaled-skip training comparisons disappear. The matched rank-collapse comparisons retain their LayerNorm, skip-connection, and identity-attention controls.

E3.justification: The removed training protocol used MSE, Adam, learning-rate selection, and 50 inputs of size 500 by 500. V2 introduces pretrained-tokenizer initialization diagnostics and an outlier-removal comparison at T = 50, 100, and 150 over depths 1–5. The layerwise-spectrum experiment's stated T changes from 100 in v1 Figure 7 to 200 in v2 Figure 6; this establishes a reported setting change without proving a rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds a direct test of whether removing additional outliers improves upon the simple fix, plus ReLU/sigmoid spectral diagnostics. It removes the Xavier/skip-scaling ablations, the single-layer gradient-width plot, the key-query gradient-depth comparison, and Appendix Figure 9's gradient-width sweeps. The main LayerNorm/skip rank-collapse analysis remains.

E5.justification: V1 Appendix A.3.1 specifies five runs per training experiment and learning-rate selection by average performance. This reporting disappears with the training study, and v2 supplies no replacement run-count or seed information. The PDFs do not establish fewer repetitions for retained experiments.

E6.justification: V2 adds BERT-family rank-collapse curves, ReLU/sigmoid spectral results, and findings that the simple fix and SVD removal have similar stable-rank behavior. It removes training losses, scaling findings, and several gradient results, and replaces the layerwise spectra under a changed stated matrix size. V1 Figure 2 and Figure 5's Markov-attention panel remain as v2 Figures 4 and 5.

T1.justification: The main bounds and proofs are retained; the standalone single-layer results largely specialize existing results, and dynamical-isometry propositions move to Appendix A.3. However, v2 Theorem 1 omits v1 Proposition 1's explicit large-d_qk qualification although its proof still requires d_qk > 16. V2's single-layer output formulas also omit the X0 factor retained in the deep-model equations, creating a dimensional inconsistency for T unequal to d.

C1.justification: The spectral-gap explanation of rank collapse and the mean-subtraction remedy remain the central contributions. V2 removes the abstract's promised training-benefit and scaling investigations and adds a contribution of interpreting centered and differential attention. Its conclusion also drops v1's explicit single-outlier qualification on the remedy's effectiveness.

C2.justification: V1 emphasizes additional outliers as a limitation of its fix and suggests removing them could improve signal propagation. V2 interprets its new comparison as showing little additional benefit and favors the inexpensive fix. It also interprets centered/differential attention through spectral-gap removal. The skip-scaling expressivity argument disappears, while the Xavier-degeneracy warning and dynamical-isometry limitation remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.4 adds the precise SVD subtraction and cutoff rule, and Figure 3 identifies the untrained models' source and use of pretrained tokenizers. Optimizer, learning-rate-grid, and trainable-parameter instructions disappear with the training study. The default architecture documentation and code-access link remain.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around alternative attention and oversmoothing. It explicitly acknowledges that Centered Self-Attention Layers uses the same subtraction and interprets Differential Transformer through the spectral gap. These and other relevant citations replace the earlier emphasis on efficient-attention alternatives and several associated references.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, experimental narrative, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. V2 separates single-layer attention analysis from the deep Markov model, moves free-probability background and dynamical-isometry discussion into Appendix A.3, and adds an appendix roadmap. The title and Random Markov terminology also change.

P2.justification: The figure collection is substantially revised: Figure 1 expands from two to four panels, a new attention-class diagram appears, and encoder and SVD-comparison plots are added. Training/scaling figures and supplementary gradient plots disappear. The layerwise-spectrum display loses its heatmaps and outlier-count annotations, while the former two-panel gradient-depth figure retains only its Markov-attention panel.

improvement.justification: V2 improves organization and attribution and adds useful encoder and outlier-removal diagnostics. These gains coexist with removed key-query gradient evidence and reduced precision in the single-layer mathematical statements. Moreover, Section 4 claims comparable gradient control although Figure 7 only plots stable rank. Removing v1's explicitly inconclusive training study also changes scope rather than clearly improving validation. These competing effects leave the net quality change uncertain.
